UNIT 03
WHERE’S EVERYTHING?
Role Play
A tourist from Sweden wants to go to the National Museum.
Tourist : Excuse me. Where is the National Museum?
Sandaru : It’s in the Main Street.
Tourist : How can I go to the Main Street?
Sandaru : Go along this road and turn left. It’s the Main Street.
Tourist : Alright.
Sandaru : There is a park on your right. Next to the park is the
Museum. It is between the park and the Art Gallery.
You can find it easily.
Tourist : Thank you very much.
Sandaru : You’re welcome. Enjoy your visit!

Plurals of Nouns
Let’s study how singular nouns form their plurals.
Most nouns form their plural form by adding -s to the singular form.
Singular (one) Plural (more than one)
a dog dogs
a boat boats
a cat cats
a song songs
the shop the shops
the tree the trees
one teacher two teachers
one book five books
When a singular noun ends with s, sh, ch or x , its plural is formed
by adding –es.
Singular (one) Plural (more than one)
a bus buses
a glass glasses
a brush brushes
a watch watches
a box boxes
Some singular nouns ending with ‘o’ also takes –es when their
plurals are formed.
Singular (one) Plural (more than one)
mango mangoes
tomato tomatoes
potato potatoes
hero heroes
Exceptions :
radio radios
studio studios

30

piano pianos
photo photos
When the last letter of a singular noun is y and the letter befor e
y is a consonant, its plural is formed by changing y to ies.
Singular (one) Plural (more than one)
baby babies
(last letter - y, consonant - b)
lady ladies
city cities
fly flies
Some nouns ending with f or fe form their plural by adding ves.
Singular (one) Plural (more than one)
leaf leaves
knife knives
life lives
calf calves
Some nouns have different singular and plural forms.
Singular (one) Plural (more than one)
man men
woman women
child children
tooth teeth
foot feet
mouse mice
